records.title: refactor(semantic-analyzer): retire the legacy reparsing WorkspaceIndex and keep cross-file state above per-file analysis
records.body:
Parent parser repository readiness: #7398 / #7400
Semantic incrementality: #2508
Canonical project facts: #4746 / #4772
Dependency inversion: #2746 / #7492

## Objective

Remove or relocate `perl-semantic-analyzer::analysis::index::WorkspaceIndex` so `perl-semantic-analyzer` has one coherent job: derive source-backed/per-file semantic contributions from accepted parser/source inputs.

Cross-file storage, document caching, invalidation, and project relationships belong to ProjectModel/live workspace/compiler-world authorities, not a second analyzer-owned workspace index that reparses text internally.

## Current contradiction

The crate README describes `perl-semantic-analyzer` as analysis over an existing AST and says cross-file lookup/document caching should pair with `perl-workspace`, but also lists `analysis::index::WorkspaceIndex` as a key entry point.

The current `WorkspaceIndex`:

- accepts URI/content directly;
- invokes `perl_parser_core::Parser` internally;
- extracts symbols/dependencies again;
- stores mutable cross-file maps;
- has its own CRUD/search behavior and tests.

Current code search found no clear production consumer outside `perl-semantic-analyzer` itself; visible references are documentation/tests. Verify that inventory before removal rather than assuming it is dead.

This shape conflicts with the accepted convergence model:

```text
accepted source/parser generation
  -> per-file semantic analysis once
  -> canonical fact/contribution output
  -> ProjectFactShard / ProjectModel + live workspace materialization
```

not:

```text
semantic analyzer
  -> read text
  -> parse again
  -> maintain another workspace index
```

## Delivery graph

### S1 — consumer/API inventory

Inventory every use of:

- `analysis::index::WorkspaceIndex`;
- its public types/methods;
- README/examples/API baselines;
- tests that preserve useful semantic behavior versus only preserving the legacy store.

Classify each as:

```text
no production consumer / retire
move to perl-workspace adapter
move to ProjectModel/query view
replace with per-file analyzer/fact API
external compatibility requiring temporary deprecation
```

### S2 — preserve useful extractors without the store

Any uniquely useful dependency/symbol extraction logic becomes deterministic per-file contribution/fact production, preferably through #2508/#4746 authorities. Do not keep a mutable workspace container merely to preserve an algorithm.

### S3 — migrate consumers and deprecate/remove public index

Move real cross-file consumers onto ProjectModel/live workspace/compiler-world APIs. Use a short compatibility window only if external-consumer evidence warrants it under the pre-1.0 policy.

### S4 — recurrence control

Add architecture proof that `perl-semantic-analyzer` cannot introduce a new source-reading/reparsing cross-file store as a shortcut around accepted parser/fact ingestion.

## Required invariants

- semantic analyzer operates on supplied accepted AST/parser/source identity, not hidden disk/text reparsing for cross-file state;
- per-file semantic contributions can be deterministic and immutable as required by #2508;
- ProjectModel/live workspace own cross-file materialization/invalidation;
- compiler-world remains separately authoritative for compile-phase cross-file semantics;
- stale generations cannot publish through a legacy analyzer cache;
- removing the index does not eliminate useful parser/semantic fixtures—move them to the correct per-file/project owner.

## Tests

- consumer inventory proves every current use is dispositioned;
- per-file symbol/dependency extraction parity for useful retained behavior;
- multi-file lookup uses ProjectModel/workspace fixture rather than analyzer-local store;
- mutation control: hidden Parser invocation inside a replacement cross-file analyzer store fails architecture policy;
- crate public API/docs no longer advertise `WorkspaceIndex` after removal/deprecation.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `perl-semantic-analyzer` has no independent canonical cross-file workspace/index authority.
- [ ] Useful semantic extraction survives as per-file/source-backed contributions or facts.
- [ ] Real cross-file consumers use ProjectModel/live workspace/compiler-world owners.
- [ ] No source is reparsed solely to maintain analyzer-owned cross-file state.
- [ ] Public API compatibility is explicitly dispositioned.
- [ ] #7398/#7400 can classify semantic analyzer as a parser/front-end package without carrying a second workspace implementation.

## Non-goals

- No semantic feature expansion.
- No ProjectModel rewrite.
- No provider cutover beyond consumers required to remove the legacy index.
- No physical parser repository move.

records.title: Heritage Track first-render, sibling-ghost scope, and automatic-geometry regressions
records.body:
# Heritage Track first-render, sibling-ghost scope, and automatic-geometry regressions

## Classification

- [ ] `fly` - minor bug: small, localized defect with limited workflow impact
- [x] `bug` - major bug: defect affecting data integrity, traceability, permissions, crashes, or important workflows
- [ ] `improvement` - minor addition: small enhancement or usability improvement without major structural changes
- [ ] `update` - major addition: new workflow, larger feature, architectural change, or cross-module extension
- [ ] `upgrade` - very large update: multi-plugin system, major architecture expansion, or long-term platform-level capability

Phase: Phase 2C follow-up  
Milestone: `0.2.3`

## Problem

Two user-visible Heritage Track regressions remain in the current 0.2.3 workflow.

### 1. First-start graph generation can fail for a valid animal

On the first Heritage use after application start, selecting **Arwen** did not generate a graph. The same Arwen-only selection worked later in the same session after other Heritage graphs had already rendered.

This indicates an initialization/order/cache/first-show dependency rather than necessarily invalid pedigree data. A valid first selection must behave the same as the same selection after Heritage has already been exercised.

### 2. Deep-scope sibling/context closure can be incomplete and Partner-normalized Denethor + Arwen can fail with `invalid geometry`

Native reproduction:

1. **Ancestors depth = 8**.
2. **Exclude archived animals = unchecked**.
3. **Denethor only** -> renders.
4. Add **Arwen** -> `Unable to render pedigree: invalid geometry`.
5. Add **Eldarion** -> renders again.

A separate native observation confirms a concrete scope defect: with **Arwen selected alone**, **Elros does not appear as a ghost**, although Arwen's father **Elrond** is already in the effective ancestor scope and Elros is Elrond's sibling.

Code review identifies the direct Arwen-only cause:

- `SelectedAnimalsStrategy` expands ancestors from explicit selections, so Arwen brings in Elrond but not Elros.
- `OffspringAndSiblingsGhostStrategy` is constructed from the explicit selected set and therefore processes Arwen, not indirectly in-scope ancestor Elrond.
- `CompositeGhostStrategy` evaluates each strategy against the same pre-expansion `display_nodes`; newly found context nodes are not staged into later family-completeness evaluation before the final union.

This is a confirmed selected-only sibling/context closure defect. The intended rule is a **bounded effective-scope context expansion**: required sibling context for animals already inside effective pedigree scope must be available, plus the missing genetic co-parent required to build that visible family, without recursively expanding unrelated ancestry/partners/descendants.

The Arwen-only scope defect and the Denethor+Arwen `invalid geometry` failure must not be conflated without evidence. In the Denethor+Arwen case, Elros should normally be a **regular ancestor of selected Denethor** through `Beth + Elros -> Denethor`. If Elros is absent there, that indicates a separate ancestor/snapshot/parent-resolution defect.

### Current leading hypothesis for the Partner-normalized `invalid geometry` failure

Chronological mode does **not** reproduce the Denethor+Arwen failure. Code analysis strongly supports a mode-specific final node/label collision rather than a rule that rejects graphs because too many relationship lines cross.

Current final frame acceptance makes surviving node/label collisions fatal. By contrast, line crossings are classified and converted into visible crossing gaps/diagnostics and are not rejected by a simple crossing-count threshold.

Relevant code paths:

- `HeritageTrackWidget._build_render_cache_entry(...)`
- `HeritageTrackWidget._render_node_collision_diagnostics(...)`
- `PedigreeRouter.node_obstacles(...)`
- router crossing/gap handling in `_find_crossing_gaps(...)` / `recompute_line_gaps(...)`

A plausible failure sequence is:

```text
Partner normalized
    -> compact row/block placement
    -> one final marker/label rectangle overlaps another
    -> collision added to fatal diagnostics
    -> candidate frame rejected
    -> generic "invalid geometry" status

Chronological
    -> date-derived Y positions provide more vertical separation
    -> same labels no longer overlap
    -> final collision validation passes
```

Adding Eldarion can change block ordering/packing enough to remove the collision, which is consistent with this hypothesis.

The exact fatal diagnostic still must be captured in the failing Partner-normalized frame before closure.

## Proposed Solution

Fix the two regressions in the existing 0.2.3 architecture without redesigning Heritage Track.

### First render

- Use the same complete initialization/snapshot/render path for the first valid graph as for later graphs.
- Base first-show geometry on initialized widget/canvas dimensions and renderer state.
- Do not require a warm-up render, hidden selection, or unrelated prior graph.
- Preserve a real localized diagnostic if the data/geometry are genuinely invalid.

### Bounded effective-scope context closure

Replace selected-only sibling expansion with a deterministic bounded rule:

```text
canonical selection
    -> normal ancestor/descendant scope
    -> for animals already in effective pedigree scope, add sibling context required by policy
    -> add missing genetic co-parent required for those visible sibling families
    -> stop at documented boundary
```

Family completeness must evaluate the appropriately expanded context, not only the original pre-ghost set.

### Partner-normalized collision recovery

If the failing diagnostic confirms a final node/label overlap, keep the final collision veto and add one **bounded deterministic semantic-block de-overlap pass before family junctions/routes are finalized**.

The recovery must:

- use the same obstacle rectangles as final validation;
- move the smallest

records.title: Desktop sessions silently archived via CTE cascade — session_key=NULL prevents resume
records.body:
## Description

Desktop sessions in the Hermes Electron app are being silently archived, making them disappear from the sidebar after restart. The sessions are NOT deleted — they remain in `state.db` with `archived=1`.

## Root Cause

Two interacting issues:

### 1. CTE cascade in `set_session_archived()` (hermes_state.py:4937-4985)

The recursive CTE walks both ancestors AND descendants through `end_reason="compression"` edges. Archiving ONE session silently archives the entire compression lineage. In my case, one trigger cascaded to 9 sessions spanning 10 days of work.

The cascade is intentional (archive the whole conversation) but there is NO confirmation dialog, NO audit log, and NO undo — the user has no idea 9 sessions just got hidden.

### 2. `session_key = NULL` on all desktop sessions

All 26 of my desktop sessions have `session_key = NULL`. The resume logic (`find_latest_gateway_session_for_peer`, line 3748) uses `session_key` as primary lookup — when NULL, the fallback gateway fields (`chat_id`, `user_id`, `chat_type`) are also NULL for desktop. Every restart creates a NEW session instead of resuming.

The stale-sibling problem is acknowledged in the source at line 5070:
> "The visible symptom is brutal: desktop resume follows the stale sibling and the user's latest messages look 'lost' even though they are persisted in the real continuation chain."

## Reproduction

1. Use Hermes desktop for several days, building compression chains
2. Trigger `set_session_archived()` on any session in the chain (sidebar click, `hermes sessions archive`, or web API)
3. All linked sessions get `archived=1`
4. Restart Hermes desktop
5. Sidebar shows empty/missing — archived sessions are hidden by default (`archived="exclude"` in the session list API)

## Evidence

- Profile: `trucks` on macOS 14.7
- 26 desktop sessions, 320 total
- 9 sessions archived in one cascade (10-14 days old, 400-1500 messages each)
- All `end_reason="compression"`, all `session_key=NULL`
- Config: `curator.archive_after_days: 90` but curator `run_count: 0` — curator never ran
- `end_session()` at line 3789 does NOT set archived — confirmed via source audit

## Suggested Fixes

1. **Short-term:** Add confirmation dialog when `set_session_archived()` would cascade to >1 session ("This will archive 9 sessions. Continue?")
2. **Root cause:** Set `session_key` for desktop sessions so the gateway can properly resolve session continuity
3. **Safety:** Add audit logging for every `set_session_archived()` call (trigger source, timestamp, cascade count)

## Workaround

```bash
# Un-archive all desktop sessions
sqlite3 ~/.hermes/profiles/trucks/state.db \
  "UPDATE sessions SET archived=0 WHERE source='desktop' AND archived=1;"
```

records.title: [RFC][pyOpenMS] Ownership model: binding policy, confirmed iterator use-after-free, and a rulebook for a full binding revamp
records.body:
Spun out of the discussion in #9777 (per @jpfeuffer's request: *"Yes, PR can be merged. Comments should be turned into an issue."*). #9777 itself landed purely additive and is not blocked by any of this.

Predecessor discussion: #4800. Related: #8855.

**Summary**

pyOpenMS decides copy-vs-alias semantics per binding rather than by policy, and the results contradict each other. 

Main issue:

**No coherent ownership policy** to apply going forward. Part VI is a normative rulebook — decision procedure, categories, numbered rules, and a grep-based audit — intended to be applied mechanically across all ~6,282 bindings in one pass.

Parts I–III establish the current state, the history, and what nanobind did and did not actually solve. Part VII covers the design options and sequencing.

---

## Status

Seven fixes are merged into `develop`: steps 1, 2 and 2b are complete, and step 3's `offsetof` hardening landed in #9815. **The ownership-policy decision — the actual subject of this issue — has been made and implemented in #9947** (in review): value semantics for element access, the Part VI-style audit executed across the full binding surface, and aliasing as an explicit opt-in under the `_view` naming contract. `src/pyOpenMS/OWNERSHIP.md` is now the normative ownership document; Part VI below stands as the rationale and audit method, not as the rulebook to apply.

| Step | Item | State |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Iterator use-after-free (Part IV) | **merged** — #9794 |
| 2 | Data arrays out of sync on sort/clear (V.1) | **merged** — #9795 |
| 2 | `set_peaks()` metadata alignment (R-6.2) | **merged** — #9808 |
| 2 | Ion mobility unit accessors mixed the two representations (V.6) | **merged** — #9809 |
| 2b | Borrowed-reference bugs (V.4) | **merged** — #9803 |
| 2b | Callback casters (R-4.7) | **merged** — #9804 |
| 3 | `offsetof` static_asserts (V.3) | **merged** — #9815 |
| 3 | `MSSpectrum::select()` parity with #9795 | **open** — #9807 |
| 3 | ~~`_view` vs `_mv` (#8855)~~ | **not open** — settled by #8857 (2026-03-10); listed here in error |
| 4–7 | Element default (copy vs alias) | **decided + implemented — #9947**: owned copies for `__getitem__`, iteration and getters; `reference_internal` removed from ~50 getters across all three binding shapes; DB singletons detached; write-back via setters/`__setitem__` |
| 4–7 | Leases (Category H) | **superseded — #9947** ships the `spectrum_view(i)` / `spectrum_views()` / `iter_spectrum_views()` view family (one per element type) instead: `reference_internal` + keep-alive + a *documented* invalidation contract (resize/sort invalidates). The full L1–L6 lease machinery (VII.3) was deliberately not built — the caveat is accepted as an explicit, named opt-in rather than defended |
| 4–7 | Bulk table view (VII.2: `peaks.erase(mask)` with aligned data arrays) | **open** — the main remaining item; `peaks_struct()` / `data_view()` keep zero-copy bulk read/write, but aligned structural ops are not built. Candidate for its own issue when this one closes |
| 4–7 | Buffer pinning | **partially covered** — equal-length replacement preserves live numpy views (#9947); general pinning not built |
| — | `SpectrumAccessOpenMSCached` wrapped; `SimpleOpenMSSpectraFactory` cached branch works | **in review — #9952** (stacked on #9947) |
| — | `ExternalProcess_test` parallel-ctest race, found while validating #9947 | spun out — #9948 |
| — | Document the thread-safety contract + the 62 GIL-release sites (R-9.5) | **open** — unblocked; general thread-safety is [out of scope](#l5-scope-decision-document-do-not-fix) |

**Decision record against Part VII.** What #9947 implements is position **A at element level with zero-copy bulk retained** under the `_view`/`_struct` names — matching C's performance claim where VII.1 shows the win actually lives (bulk), without C's lease machinery or per-element view-class explosion. The naming carries the contract: `get_*` always returns an owned copy; aliasing accessors never take the `get_` prefix and end in `_view`/`_views`/`_struct`. Element views measure ~120× over copying iteration on peak-heavy experiments. The documented exceptions (fluent builders, DB-singleton lookups, shared-pointer data models including the OpenSwath interchange types) live in OWNERSHIP.md. One alternative was evaluated and deferred: nanobind-property attribute chaining (`exp.spectra[0].rt = 5.0`) — capability-equivalent to views, but the attribute spelling hides the aliasing hazard the `_view` name deliberately marks, and it requires per-container proxy classes rather than plain properties (vector type casters copy). Revisit post-release with usage evidence.

#9808 also added a writable ion mobility dimension (`set_peaks(..., ion_mobility=...)`, `set_drift_time_array()`), named through `IMDataConverter::setIMUnit()` so what is written is what `getIMData()` reads back and what survives an mzML round-trip.

Six lessons from the fixes so far, all of which affect how a binding audit must be run:

1. **`keep_alive` does not secure a retained raw pointer when the receiver is copyable** — the C++ copy duplicates the pointer without the Python-side edge (V.4). Guarantee process lifetime instead.
2. **A `.def("name", [](...)`-only grep is not an audit** — it missed 9 constructor registrations. Grep `nb::init<` too.
3. **`OPENMS_PRECONDITION` compiles to nothing in release builds** — bounds checks written with it do not protect the bindings.
4. **The audit surface is wider than ownership.** V.6/#9809 — an accessor that guarded on one ion mobility representation and returned the other — is a correctness defect that none of the VI.11 greps would have surfaced. It was found by reading the file while implementing R-6.2.
5. **The presence of guards is not evidence that the thing at risk is guarded.** The four `static_assert`s over `Peak1D` looked like a deliberate ABI contract and constrained everything *except* the two byte offsets the dtype actually depends on (V.3). Coun

records.body:
**Languages:** cpp

# Graphs (Path Existence)

## Video Solution

For more details about **Find if Path Exists in Graph**, watch the walkthrough at [resources](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=knLFe7hEp3Y)

## Concept

To determine whether a path exists between two vertices in an undirected graph we can **traverse** the graph starting from the source vertex and see if we ever reach the destination.  
The traversal can be done with **Breadth‑First Search (BFS)** or **Depth‑First Search (DFS)**. Both visit each vertex at most once, using a `visited` array to avoid infinite loops caused by cycles.

A real‑world analogy: imagine you are in a maze of rooms (vertices) connected by doors (edges). You start in the source room and keep opening doors to new rooms you haven’t entered yet. If you ever step into the destination room, a path exists; if you run out of unopened doors without reaching it, there is no path.

## When to Use It

Use graph traversal (BFS/DFS) when you see:
- The problem asks whether a **path** or **connection** exists between two nodes.
- The graph is given as an edge list (or adjacency list) and is **undirected**.
- You need to check **reachability** or **connected components**.
- Constraints are large (up to 2·10⁵ vertices/edges) → an O(V+E) solution is required.

## Template

Here is a reusable Python template for BFS‑based reachability checking. Replace the `process` comment with any per‑node logic you need.

```python
from collections import deque
from typing import List

def has_path(n: int, edges: List[List[int]], source: int, destination: int) -> bool:
    # 1️⃣ Build adjacency list
    adj = [[] for _ in range(n)]
    for u, v in edges:
        adj[u].append(v)
        adj[v].append(u)

    # 2️⃣ BFS traversal
    visited = [False] * n
    q = deque([source])
    visited[source] = True

    while q:
        node = q.popleft()
        if node == destination:          # 🎯 Destination reached
            return True
        for nei in adj[node]:            # Explore neighbours
            if not visited[nei]:
                visited[nei] = True
                q.append(nei)

    # 3️⃣ Exhausted all reachable vertices without finding destination
    return False
```

## LeetCode Problem Walkthrough

### Problem: 1971. Find if Path Exists in Graph
https://leetcode.com/problems/find-if-path-exists-in-graph/

---

### Approach 1: Brute Force (Naïve DFS without visited)

**Algorithm**  
Start a recursive DFS from `source`. At each step, recursively explore every neighbour **without** marking vertices as visited. If we ever hit `destination`, return `True`. If recursion exhausts all paths, return `False`.  
Because we never mark visited nodes, the algorithm may revisit the same vertex many times, leading to exponential blow‑up and infinite recursion on cycles.

**Implementation**

```python
class Solution:
    def validPath(self, n: int, edges: List[List[int]], source: int, destination: int) -> bool:
        # Build adjacency list
        adj = [[] for _ in range(n)]
        for u, v in edges:
            adj[u].append(v)
            adj[v].append(u)

        def dfs(cur: int) -> bool:
            if cur == destination:
                return True
            # Explore all neighbours (no visited check!)
            for nxt in adj[cur]:
                if dfs(nxt):
                    return True
            return False

        return dfs(source)
```

**Complexity Analysis**  
- Time complexity: O(2^V) in the worst case (each vertex can be chosen or not in a path) → exponential.  
- Space complexity: O(V) for the recursion stack (plus adjacency list O(V+E)).

---

### Approach 2: BFS with Visited Set (Optimal Traversal)

**Intuition**  
Marking a vertex as visited the first time we see it guarantees we never process the same vertex twice. This turns the naïve exponential search into a linear‑time graph traversal because each edge is examined at most once.

**Algorithm**  
1. Build an adjacency list from the edge list.  
2. Initialize a queue with the `source` and a `visited` boolean array.  
3. While the queue is not empty: pop a vertex, if it is the `destination` return `True`; otherwise push all unvisited neighbours onto the queue and mark them visited.  
4. If the queue empties without finding the destination, return `False`.

**Implementation**

```python
from collections import deque
from typing import List

class Solution:
    def validPath(self, n: int, edges: List[List[int]], source: int, destination: int) -> bool:
        # 1️⃣ Adjacency list
        adj = [[] for _ in range(n)]
        for u, v in edges:
            adj[u].append(v)
            adj[v].append(u)

        # 2️⃣ BFS
        visited = [False] * n
        q = deque([source])
        visited[source] = True

        while q:
            node = q.popleft()
            if node == destination:
                return True
            for nei in adj[node]:
                if not visited[nei]:
                    visited[nei] = True
                    q.append(nei)

        return False
```

**Complexity Analysis**  
- Time complexity: O(V + E) — each vertex is enqueued at most once and each edge inspected twice (once from each endpoint).  
- Space complexity: O(V + E) for the adjacency list + O(V) for the `visited` array and queue.

---

### Approach 3: Union‑Find (Disjoint Set Union)

**Intuition**  
If two vertices belong to the same connected component, there exists a path between them. Union‑Find efficiently merges edges into components and can answer “are source and destination in the same set?” in near‑constant time.

**Algorithm**  
1. Initialize each vertex as its own parent.  
2. For every edge `[u, v]`, union the sets containing `u` and `v`.  
3. After processing all edges, check if `find(source) == find(destination)`.  
   - Path compression and union by rank/size keep operations almost O(1).

records.title: Archive and restore without losing context
records.body:
## Outcome

Hide material from daily views while retaining recoverability.

## Contribution

Vertical slice 7 of #1: Core: Capture and organize durable text notes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Both clients archive/restore using target revisions; ordinary restore removes the direct user cause without duplicate direct-user archive causes.
- [ ] Origin causes are stored once and inherited through ancestry; restoring ancestors preserves independent descendant causes.
- [ ] List/search exclude effectively archived entities by default with explicit inclusion; Get remains available with computed archived status and cause explanation.
- [ ] Archived entities reject updates; archived destinations reject creation and moves.
- [ ] Inherited-only archived entities can relocate, optionally renaming, to active parents; directly archived entities must restore before moving.
- [ ] Archive/restore stay available under lifecycle rules; all eligibility/constraints are validated atomically and descendants need not supply revisions.
- [ ] Archived siblings reserve slugs. No delete operation is added.
- [ ] Active-project views omit archived projects without clearing selection; restoration makes selected projects eligible again.

## Implementation context and exclusions

All affected client flows and prior routes must adopt lifecycle behavior. Get target revision alone cannot detect changed ancestor archive state; validate effective state transactionally. General extension hooks/causes SDK remains deferred, but schema/semantics must not preclude independent causes.

## Context

Architecture and authority live in [docs/architecture](https://github.com/YourTechBudStudio/Raphael/tree/main/docs/architecture) and [ADRs](https://github.com/YourTechBudStudio/Raphael/tree/main/docs/adrs). Read the parent epic and relevant records before implementation. This epic explicitly supersedes the initial Turso/Tantivy direction with mature SQLite + FTS5; the runtime document may still need alignment. Implement capabilities vertically, with server-backed parity between mobile and CLI, not identical client interactions. No bulk mutations or pluggable CLI.

## Archive cause schema and retrieval

Conceptual storage (names are illustrative):

```text
nodes(id, type, parent_id, slug, revision, ...common content...)
archive_causes(id, node_id, owner, reason_key, created_at)
UNIQUE(node_id, owner, reason_key)
```

`owner` is user or extension identity; ordinary user reason_key is a fixed direct marker, avoiding multiple user causes from repeated archive requests. Store explicit causes only at origins, not inherited rows per descendant. Effective archived is true if target or any ancestor has an active cause. Derive with recursive SQL through current parentage; no independent archived boolean authority. Get returns computed boolean plus origins explaining blockers. Get Path remains explicit. Ordinary client restore need not expose a --cause selection: it removes target's direct user reason, not inherited causes or extension-controlled reasons. Exact behavior when no direct user cause exists (no-op versus explicit outcome) still needs final contract choice; never imply entity is active when reasons remain.

Example: project 10 has cause B; child 12 has independent cause A; child 11 has none. All appear archived. Restoring 10 removes B only: 10 and 11 active, 12 still archived. Removing internal cause records is not deleting user content; no audit-event retention policy was specified. An extension controls withdrawal of its own reasons in future #13.

## Operations and invariants

```sh
raphael archive /work/backend --revision 7
raphael restore /work/backend --revision 8
```

Use POST /api/nodes/archive and /restore, shared target selectors and revision. Return the saved target/new revision and truthful effective state, not a blanket success-means-active interpretation. Descendant cause inheritance is core-owned; callers don't enumerate descendant revisions and ancestor archive need not bump each descendant's revision. Therefore check ancestry/current destination inside every relevant mutation transaction.

Active targets permit normal edits/moves. Inherited-only archived targets forbid edits but permit extraction into an active parent (with optional rename). Targets with any direct cause cannot move/update. Restore and adding an independent archive cause remain possible while already archived. Root is not archivable. Creation and moves into archived parents reject. Scoped lists/search must apply effective archive rules even if scope starts inside an archived subtree; don't merely inspect target-local causes. Explicit archive inclusion doesn't relax mutation rules. Active-project selection remains stored when hidden by archive. Current-ancestry inheritance makes extracted inherited-only material active naturally; no materialized cascade cleanup or forced active flags.

records.title: Tasks: allow subtasks deeper than one level
records.body:
`MAX_TASK_DEPTH = 1` in `src/lib/tasks.ts` is the only thing enforcing a single level of nesting. The schema never had an opinion — `tasks.parentId` is an ordinary self-reference and the queries that walk it are recursive.

Groundwork already done so this stays small:
- the constant lives in one place, referenced only by the indent and move validators
- `depth` is maintained on write
- the server sends a flat row list and the client assembles the tree
- subtree operations (delete, move, complete-cascade) use recursive CTEs and already work at any depth
- rows indent from their position in the rendered tree, not their stored depth

So the change is the constant, the drag-target maths, and checking the indent affordance offers the extra level.

records.title: Cache invalidation on local dependencies when using docker
records.body:
<!--
Thank you for taking the time to report an issue! We're glad to have you involved with uv.

If you're filing a bug report, please consider including the following information:

* A minimal code snippet that reproduces the bug.
* The command you invoked (e.g., `uv pip sync requirements.txt`), ideally including the `--verbose` flag.
* The current uv platform.
* The current uv version (`uv --version`).
-->

Hello.

I am having difficulties using uv in docker. My project structure has two python libraries, one is an API server, and the other is an internal library.
The problem I am encountering is that after building, when running the image, the `uv run` reinstalls my internal libraries, with the following message: `Requirement installed, but not fresh: ...`. This is problematic, because as per docker best practices, it is good to ensure that the install actually happens on the build stage, and not in the actual running phase of my application.
When debugging the issue further, I found out that it happens because the ctime of my `pyproject.toml` of the internal library changes between the docker build and the actual run.

I finally validated that symptom using the following dockerfile:
```
FROM ubuntu:22.04

RUN touch a && stat a > /root/stat-a
RUN sleep 5
```
And running: `docker build --no-cache . -t playground && docker run playground sh -c 'cat /root/stat-a && stat a'`
The output that I received was: 
```
  File: a
  Size: 0               Blocks: 0          IO Block: 4096   regular empty file
Device: e3h/227d        Inode: 1336246     Links: 1
Access: (0644/-rw-r--r--)  Uid: (    0/    root)   Gid: (    0/    root)
Access: 2024-11-18 10:04:52.462498005 +0000
Modify: 2024-11-18 10:04:52.462498005 +0000
Change: 2024-11-18 10:04:52.462498005 +0000
 Birth: 2024-11-18 10:04:52.462498005 +0000
---
  File: a
  Size: 0               Blocks: 0          IO Block: 4096   regular empty file
Device: e3h/227d        Inode: 225316      Links: 1
Access: (0644/-rw-r--r--)  Uid: (    0/    root)   Gid: (    0/    root)
Access: 2024-11-18 10:04:52.000000000 +0000
Modify: 2024-11-18 10:04:52.000000000 +0000
Change: 2024-11-18 10:04:57.680498008 +0000
 Birth: 2024-11-18 10:04:57.680498008 +0000
```

As seen, two things are changing between the build and run - both the inode number, and the Change & Birth times.
This seems like an odd behavior of docker, but as I dived deeper it seems inherent to the layering system of docker.

I think that the solution to that issue should come from uv's side, as the usage for similar type of projects in docker should be very common.

A possible approach that would solve both the cache freshness problem and would work with docker's odd behavior would be using checksums for local dependencies freshness check.

Some additional information:
- uv version: v0.5.1
- Platform: MacOS with Docker Desktop

Thanks in advance!
Yannay

records.title: PRD01-SUB07-PLAN03: Implement Chart of Accounts REST API Endpoints

## Overview

This implementation plan delivers the RESTful API layer for Chart of Accounts management, exposing account operations via versioned endpoints (`/api/v1/accounts`). It implements API controllers using Laravel route attributes, Form Requests for validation, API Resources for response transformation, and specialized endpoints for tree operations, search, and bulk operations.

**Prerequisites:**
- ✅ Must complete #108 (PRD01-SUB07-PLAN01: COA Foundation) first

records.title: PRD01-SUB13-PLAN01: Implement Employee Management Foundation
records.body:
## Overview

Implement core employee management with UUID-based records, AES-256 encryption for sensitive data, organizational hierarchy tracking, and employment lifecycle management supporting 100,000+ employees per tenant.

## Requirements

**Functional Requirements:**
- FR-HCM-001: Employee master data with personal information, employment details, and encrypted sensitive fields (SSN, national ID)
- FR-HCM-002: Organizational hierarchy with self-referencing manager relationships and recursive queries
- FR-HCM-003: Employee lifecycle workflows: hire, transfer, promotion, termination with validation
- FR-HCM-004: Automatic employment history tracking for all lifecycle events
- FR-HCM-005: Support for multiple employment types (Full-time, Part-time, Contract, Intern)

**Business Rules:**
- BR-HCM-001: Cannot delete employee if payroll or leave history exists
- BR-HCM-002: Employee number must be unique per tenant
- BR-HCM-003: Cannot terminate employee with active leave requests

**Performance Requirements:**
- PR-HCM-001: Employee retrieval < 200ms (with relationships)
- PR-HCM-002: Hierarchy queries < 100ms for 10,000+ employees

**Scalability:**
- SCR-HCM-001: Support 100,000+ employees per tenant

**Compliance:**
- CR-HCM-001: GDPR right to erasure (anonymization)
- CR-HCM-002: Encrypted storage for SSN and national ID (AES-256)

## Implementation Goals

### GOAL-001: Create Employee and Employment History Database Schema
**Tasks:**
- TASK-001: Create employees table with UUID primary key, encrypted SSN/national_id, self-referencing manager_id
- TASK-002: Add unique composite index on (tenant_id, employee_number)
- TASK-003: Add foreign key to tenants, departments, positions tables
- TASK-004: Add soft deletes support with deleted_at timestamp
- TASK-005: Create employment_history table for lifecycle tracking
- TASK-006: Add indexes on employment_history (employee_id, event_type, event_date)
- TASK-007: Add CHECK constraints (hire_date not in future, termination_date > hire_date)
- TASK-008: Add manager_id FK constraint with ON DELETE SET NULL
- TASK-009: Document schema in migration file with comprehensive comments

### GOAL-002: Create Employee Model with Encryption and Status Management
**Tasks:**
- TASK-010: Create Employee model with BelongsToTenant, HasUuids, SoftDeletes, LogsActivity traits
- TASK-011: Create EmployeeStatus enum (ACTIVE, TERMINATED, SUSPENDED)
- TASK-012: Create EmploymentType enum (FULL_TIME, PART_TIME, CONTRACT, INTERN) with isEligibleForBenefits()
- TASK-013: Create EmploymentEventType enum (HIRE, TRANSFER, PROMOTION, DEMOTION, SALARY_ADJUSTMENT, TERMINATION)
- TASK-014: Add encrypted accessors/mutators for SSN and national_id fields
- TASK-015: Add computed attribute getFullNameAttribute() concatenating first+last+middle names
- TASK-016: Add computed attribute getTenureYearsAttribute() calculating years since hire_date
- TASK-017: Configure activity logging to track name, status, department, position changes
- TASK-018: Add $hidden array to exclude encrypted fields from API responses
- TASK-019: Implement anonymize() method for GDPR compliance (replace with "Anonymous")
- TASK-020: Add canBeDeleted() method checking for payroll/leave history
- TASK-021: Add relationships: tenant(), manager(), directReports(), employmentHistory()
- TASK-022: Add scopeActive() query scope filtering by EmployeeStatus::ACTIVE
- TASK-023: Configure factory with 10 states (active, terminated, suspended, with_manager, etc.)
- TASK-024: Add PHPDoc blocks with @property annotations for all virtual attributes

### GOAL-003: Implement Employee Repository with Hierarchy Queries
**Tasks:**
- TASK-025: Create EmployeeRepositoryContract with 10 required methods
- TASK-026: Create DatabaseEmployeeRepository implementing contract
- TASK-027: Implement findById($id) with eager loading (tenant, department, position, manager)
- TASK-028: Implement findByEmail($email, $tenantId) with tenant scope
- TASK-029: Implement findByEmployeeNumber($number, $tenantId) with unique validation
- TASK-030: Implement getDirectReports($employeeId) returning immediate subordinates
- TASK-031: Implement getAllSubordinates($employeeId) using recursive CTE query
- TASK-032: Implement getOrganizationalHierarchy($tenantId) returning full tree structure
- TASK-033: Add Redis caching for hierarchy queries with 15-minute TTL (GUD-005)

### GOAL-004: Implement Employee Lifecycle Actions
**Tasks:**
- TASK-034: Create HireEmployeeAction with AsAction trait
- TASK-035: Validate unique employee_number per tenant (BR-HCM-002)
- TASK-036: Validate hire_date not in future (CON-002)
- TASK-037: Create employee record with status ACTIVE
- TASK-038: Dispatch EmployeeHiredEvent with employee, hire_date, initial_salary
- TASK-039: Log activity "Employee hired" with created_by context

- TASK-040: Create TransferEmployeeAction with AsAction trait
- TASK-041: Validate new department/position exists and belongs to tenant
- TASK-042: Update employee department_id, position_id, effective_date
- TASK-043: Dispatch EmployeeTransferredEvent with old/new department/position
- TASK-044: Clear hierarchy cache on manager/department change (GUD-005)

- TASK-045: Create TerminateEmployeeAction with AsAction trait
- TASK-046: Validate termination_date > hire_date (CON-003)
- TASK-047: Check for active leave requests (BR-HCM-003)
- TASK-048: Update status to TERMINATED, set termination_date and reason
- TASK-049: Dispatch EmployeeTerminatedEvent with termination details

- TASK-050: Add custom exceptions: DuplicateEmployeeNumberException, InvalidHireDateException, etc.
- TASK-051: Add comprehensive validation messages and error codes

### GOAL-005: Implement Employee History Tracking Model and Observer
**Tasks:**
- TASK-052: Create EmployeeEmploymentHistory model with BelongsToTenant trait
- TASK-053: Add relationships: employee(), performedBy() (user who made change)
- TASK-054: Add encrypted accessor/mutator for salary field in history
